verdict.rationale: Obsidian's own architecture keeps notes as local plain-text Markdown files, and the docs say users have 'total control over your data'. Selective sync controls which files reach Obsidian's servers, and a community user confirms notes stay only on their machine and sync service. There are no documented retention or deletion controls, such as purging remote Sync data, setting version-history retention windows, or account deletion. Missing for 10: documented Sync/Publish data retention periods, remote vault or version-history deletion controls, account/data deletion process, independent corroboration of deletion behavior.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can control data retention and deletion

citations.quote: You have total control over your data, which means you can use Obsidian offline and switch to another app easily
Because notes are plain text files, you can use other text editors and file managers to edit and manage notes.
Selective sync - Configure which files and settings to sync.
Version history - View or restore previous versions of a note.
